subject: HealthWave: sudden token-denied cascade (429) during nightly sync
messages:
From: Sara Liang <sara.liang@healthwave.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@healthwave.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden 429 cascade during nightly sync — urgent

Hi Rachel,

We started seeing a massive spike of 429s around 02:12 UTC during our nightly patient-sync window. Thousands of requests are being rejected (429 / token denied) and our workers have started exponential backoff which is causing timeouts and overall sync slowness. This is the first time we've seen an issue of this magnitude from Redwood in production.

We attached a small sample of traces and timestamps (healthwave_trace_0914.zip). Please advise urgently — this is breaking our SLA for tonight's deliveries.

Quick details:
- Org: healthwave-org (tenant id: hw-1211)
- Affected flows: /v1/generate bulk sync job; peak concurrency ~1200 rps
- Errors: primarily 429, some 504s as backoff cascades

Please escalate to engineering and let me know if you need additional logs.

Sara Liang
Head of Platform
HealthWave Inc.
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liang <sara.liang@healthwave.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 429 cascade during nightly sync — urgent

Sara —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and the traces. I'm escalating immediately to our sRE and product teams. First-cut ask: can you confirm whether you recently changed org/project tokens or introduced a new project alias? We have seen similar patterns when tiering or project mapping flips and the rate limiter assigns an unexpectedly low bucket.

I have opened CASE-12849 and attached your trace bundle there. Our priority now is to reduce customer-facing 429s while we diagnose the root cause. We'll propose a short mitigation within the next 20–30 minutes.

I'll update you as soon as we have a temporary rule in place.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim | Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0134
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: HealthWave 429 cascade — needs infra playbook

Folks — forwarding HealthWave's report. Quick read: heavy 429s and cascading retries during their nightly sync. Rachel suspects tier/alias change.

Immediate goals:
1) Apply an emergency throttle override to hw-1211 (raise project bucket temporarily) — ben, can you coordinate with infra ops?
2) Disable aggressive client-side retry guidance for this tenant via the Console (reduce retries to 2) — jonas, can you push a policy patch?
3) Confirm whether last night's config rollout included organ->project alias remapping (product / rollout logs) — Rachel, can you pull the rollout id?
4) Exec loop: prepare a 1-paragraph incident summary for the CRO and CS lead.

I attached: request-sla-exception-0914.pdf with suggested customer communication language. We'll need to be crisp — customer is already concerned about SLA impact.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success (Escalations), Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rachel.kim@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: HealthWave 429 cascade — needs infra playbook

On it — quick status: infra confirmed the rate limiter saw hw-1211 assigned to the "starter-tier" token pool after the midnight rollout. That pool only allows 600 concurrent token slots which is ~half of their expected capacity. Preliminary hypothesis: a label mismatch in the org->project mapping caused the downgrade.

Immediate actions taken (10:30–10:36 PDT):
- Temporarily bumped hw-1211 to a higher concurrency bucket (provisional override) — this should reduce 429s within ~2 minutes.
- Applied a soft-rate-cap on client-retries for the tenant via Console (max retries = 2, 30s backoff).
- Captured detailed rate-limiter logs and created JIRA RI-8732 for permanent remediation (mapping logic fix + added unit tests).

Next steps:
- Product to review rollout artifact for alias mapping & pin the correct mapping (Jonas and Product).
- Ask PM for a postmortem and communication to HealthWave ops with timeline and credit options.

Ben Carter
Sr. Technical Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 510-555-0122
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liang <sara.liang@healthwave.com>, ops@healthwave.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden 429 cascade during nightly sync — urgent

Sara — quick update and apologies for the disruption.

What happened (short): during a midnight rollout a label mismatch caused hw-1211 to be assigned to a lower concurrency bucket (starter-tier) instead of their expected production tier. That produced a surge of 429s which then caused large retry backoffs and some timeouts.

What we did (mitigation):
- Temporarily increased hw-1211 concurrency bucket (immediate fix)
- Limited client-side retries to prevent retry storms
- Opened JIRA RI-8732 to fix the mapping logic and added assertions to the rollout tests

Items we will follow up on:
- Root cause postmortem (by Friday, 2027-09-17)
- Incident timeline + remarks for execs and customer success
- Proposal for service credit for the impacted window (we'll include options)

If you can confirm whether you changed any tokens/aliases on your side in the last 48 hours it will help accelerate the postmortem. We'll share the logs we captured to CASE-12849 and can jump on a call if helpful.

Again, sorry for the outage. We're treating this as a high-priority postmortem and remediation.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim | Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0134
